html:
Thessaloniki is a port city of northern Greece, on the Thermaic Gulf, and the second city of Greece. For most of its history it was the second city of the empire that ruled it.

King Cassander of Macedon founded it in about 315 BCE and named it after his wife Thessalonike, half-sister of Alexander the Great; see the kingdom of Cassander. Under Rome it stood on the Via Egnatia, the road from the Adriatic to Byzantium, and the apostle Paul wrote letters to its Christians. Around 300 the emperor Galerius made it his capital and built an arch and the round Rotunda there. The Edict of Thessalonica of 380 made Nicene Christianity the faith of the empire.

In the Byzantine centuries it was the empire's "co-capital". The brothers Cyril and Methodius, who took writing to the Slavs, came from here; see their mission to Moravia. The Normans sacked it in 1185. In the 1300s it was the home of the theologian Gregory Palamas and of the Hexabiblos law book, and a rebel group, the Zealots, ruled it for a few years during the civil war.

The Ottomans took it in 1430. After the expulsion of the Jews from Spain in 1492, many Sephardic Jews settled here, and for four centuries Jews were the largest group in the city. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk was born here in 1881. Greece took the city in 1912. In 1943 the German occupiers deported almost all of its Jews to Auschwitz.
sum: Thessaloniki is a port city of northern Greece, on the Thermaic Gulf, and the second city of Greece. For most of its history it was the second city of the empire that ruled it.
